Summary: Review literature findings and define the Qadam research gap
Acceptance criteria: Read four core papers; identify methods, findings, limitations and source sections. Connect a bounded business-to-student gap to Qadam design choices. Separate proposed benefits from measured outcomes.

Summary: Validate the ERD against current database migrations
Acceptance criteria: Check Task, Team, Proposal, Milestone and Progress award keys and multiplicities against migrations. Keep future User identity visibly proposed. Explain JSONB snapshots and existing ownership limitations.

Summary: Review activity and sequence diagrams for task formulation
Acceptance criteria: Trace draft creation, clarification, assembly, human correction, confirmation and optional publication. Verify API paths, revision checks, database writes and manual failure paths. Every member must explain the flow.

Summary: Finalize the manual versus AI evaluation protocol
Acceptance criteria: Freeze matched scenarios, same manual/AI form, six paired business participants and balanced order. Define time, five-dimension quality rubric, unsupported facts and error reporting. Use two independent assessors; preserve incomplete attempts. No results may be invented.

Summary: Publish and review the ongoing AI work
Acceptance criteria: User confirms AI development is underway outside the repository. Publish actual changes under Mereke own account, describe provider/prompt decisions, add meaningful validation and obtain review. Do not attribute existing initial AI commits to Mereke.
Evidence: AI pull request; tests; prompt/version notes

Summary: Verify frontend review and correction before confirmation
Acceptance criteria: Check generated question display, editable candidates, provenance labels, manual fallback and confirmation. Show that unconfirmed edits do not replace a published snapshot. Record browser evidence with synthetic data.

Summary: Run database and API integrity checks
Acceptance criteria: Run fresh tests using an isolated test database. Verify revision conflicts, actor checks, private drafts, proposal decisions and one-time milestone points. Record commands and actual outcomes; skipped tests are not passes.

Summary: Confirm individual contributions and remaining responsibilities
Acceptance criteria: Each member reviews their actual Git contributions and work outside Git. Confirm Bekasyl frontend/integration, Mereke AI, Zere backend/database. Link evidence and identify future responsibilities separately from completed work.

Summary: Arrange the supervisor meeting around 21 October
Acceptance criteria: Send a professional greeting and request an exact meeting time through the normal channel. Share revised materials and questions. Record agreed date and outcome. First pre-defense is approved, but the meeting and signed form are not yet confirmed.

Summary: Collect genuine user discussions and pilot recruitment agreements
Acceptance criteria: Conduct 3-5 real discussions or document a substantive stakeholder agreement. Obtain consent and keep identifying information private. Record supporting and contradictory evidence. Confirm feasibility of the later six-person comparison.

Summary: Prepare and rehearse the architecture and research presentation
Acceptance criteria: Use the revised report and diagrams. Each member explains personal decisions and one relevant paper. Demonstrate live or explicitly manual AI behavior and distinguish historical verification from current results. Rehearse committee questions.

Summary: Review and submit the first pre-defense package
Acceptance criteria: Apply meeting corrections, inspect the Word export and repository links, confirm each contribution, collect the signed approval form through the university procedure and submit the required files. Record actual submission evidence. Approval is not proof of submission.
Evidence: Final report; submission receipt; approval form
